Dockerfile.text:
FROM node:22-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY survey.mjs render.mjs server.mjs ./
RUN mkdir -p /data && chown node /data
USER node
ENV PORT=8080 STATE=/tmp/state.json TRUST_PROXY=false
EXPOSE 8080
HEALTHCHECK CMD wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz || exit 1
CMD ["node", "server.mjs"]

README.md.text:
# Survey Keeper

After using this, you can now **run a survey or an NPS check on a server you own**, read the score with a 95% range instead of a bare number, see which words detractors use more than promoters, compare channels, and get a message the moment someone scores you 0 to 6, instead of paying a survey service per response.

**Live tool:** https://duncan-haywood.github.io/monorepo-projects/survey-keeper/

Two parts, both free and MIT:

- **`index.html`**: paste scores and comments, see the NPS, its range and the word table. Runs in the browser; nothing is uploaded.
- **`server.mjs`**: one Node process, **zero dependencies**, state in one JSON file. Public survey pages, admin, results, CSV export, a webhook on every detractor.

## Why someone would use this

| Today | Cost / catch | Survey Keeper |
|---|---|---|
| Typeform, SurveyMonkey, Delighted, Survicate, Refiner | Monthly fee that rises with responses; answers live with them; trend and export sit on higher tiers | Your server, unlimited surveys and responses, no fee per response |
| LimeSurvey, Formbricks | Full platforms: a database, a build, many settings | One Node process and one JSON file |
| A Google Form plus a spreadsheet | No NPS maths, no range, no per-channel score, no alert when a customer is unhappy | NPS with a 95% range, results by source, a webhook on every detractor |

Honest limits: no skip logic or page branching, no email sending (share the link, or embed it), one admin key, no respondent panel or quota control, and the word table is counting, not sentiment analysis. Answers are anonymous by design, so you cannot reply to a detractor unless they typed a way to reach them into a comment. For research-grade surveys use a full platform.

## How it works

1. **Define a survey** at `/admin/new`, one question per line: `type: label | option | option`. Types are `nps` (0 to 10), `rating` (1 to 5), `single`, `multi` and `text`. A star after the type (`nps*`) makes it required.

   ```
   nps*: How likely are you to recommend us to a friend or colleague?
   text: What is the main reason for your score?
   rating: How easy was it to get started?
   single: How often do you use us? | Daily | Weekly | Monthly | Rarely
   multi: Which features matter most to you? | Search | Export | Integrations
   ```

2. **Share the link** `/s/<name>`. Add `?ref=email`, `?ref=app` or `?ref=invoice` to tag the channel; results show a score for each. Or embed it: set `EMBED_ORIGINS` to the origins allowed to frame it, then use the iframe snippet on the results page.
3. **Read the results** at `/admin/s/<id>/results`: the NPS (promoters 9-10, passives 7-8, detractors 0-6) with a 95% range from the variance of the three-point score, the score distribution, a day-by-day table, option shares, rating averages, and for each text question the words people mention and whether detractors or promoters say them more often.
4. **Close the loop.** Set `ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL` (a Slack or Discord incoming-webhook URL, https only) and every response that scores 0 to 6 posts the score, the channel and the first comment.
5. **Take the data with you.** CSV per survey (spreadsheet-formula safe) and a JSON export of everything.

A survey with responses keeps its question types and options fixed so old answers can never be re-mapped to different questions; labels, title and thank-you text stay editable.

## Reading an NPS honestly

With 20 answers a score of +30 has a range of roughly -10 to +70, so do not celebrate or panic over a few points. The results page prints the range beside the score and warns below 30 answers. NPS also depends on who answers: a survey sent only to active users reads higher than one sent to everyone who signed up.

## Run it

```sh
cd ventures/survey-keeper
node --test        # no network
ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) node server.mjs
```

Open `http://localhost:8080/admin` (any user name, `ADMIN_KEY` as the password). Settings: `STATE` (JSON file path; keep it on a persistent disk), `PORT`, `PUBLIC_URL` (https, used for links shown in the admin), `TRUST_PROXY=true` behind a proxy so rate limiting sees real client addresses, `ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL`, `EMBED_ORIGINS`, `HIDE_SPONSOR_LINK=true`.

## One-click deploy

Fork the repository, then open `https://render.com/deploy?repo=<your fork URL>`. Render builds the Dockerfile in **your** account with a 1 GB disk and generates `ADMIN_KEY`. Nothing runs on the author's accounts. Serve it over HTTPS only (Render does); the admin uses HTTP Basic auth. `docker-compose.yml` runs it on any box with Docker; Fly.io steps are at the top of `fly.toml`.

## What it stores

Survey definitions and, for each response, the answers, a timestamp and an optional short source tag. No name, email or IP address is stored unless a respondent types one into a comment. IP addresses are kept in memory only for rate limiting (10 submissions a minute per address). A hidden honeypot field quietly drops simple bots.

## Disclaimer

No warranty; no uptime or delivery guarantee. You operate the survey and are responsible for its questions, your privacy notice and the consent and data-protection rules where you and your respondents live. Scores, ranges and word tables are heuristics and depend on who answers. Not legal, tax or financial advice. MIT licensed. If it saves you a subscription, you can [sponsor the author](https://github.com/sponsors/Duncan-Haywood).

VENTURE.yaml.text:
name: survey-keeper
description: >-
  Self-hosted surveys and Net Promoter Score (Typeform / SurveyMonkey /
  Delighted alternative): NPS, rating, choice and free-text questions from a
  plain-text definition, a 95% range on every NPS, the words detractors use
  more than promoters, results by source, CSV export and an alert on every
  detractor. Zero-dependency server, embeddable, one-click Render deploy.
stage: prototype
owner: duncan

# Screened 2026-10-17. Paid market proven: Typeform, SurveyMonkey, Delighted,
# Survicate, Refiner and Hotjar Surveys charge $25-300 a month, and the cheap
# tiers cap responses or hide NPS trend and export. Open-source options
# (LimeSurvey, Formbricks) are full platforms: a database, a build, many
# settings. The gap is a one-process NPS and survey server that also says
# *why* the score is what it is (detractor-heavy words) and pings you on every
# detractor so the loop gets closed. Pairs with help-keeper, feedback-board and
# support-desk. duplicate_check: grep of ventures/ on 2026-10-17 found no
# survey or NPS server (form-inbox collects website forms, not scored surveys).
#
# First visitor: r/selfhosted, r/SaaS, Indie Hackers: "self hosted NPS survey",
# "typeform alternative open source", "delighted alternative".
# Path to revenue (payments stay off): free MIT lead magnet; done-for-you setup
# and sponsors; hosting under the public name is owner-gated.

hypotheses:
  - claim: >-
      Small SaaS owners will deploy their own NPS survey when it shows a
      confidence range and the words detractors use, because a bare score from
      30 answers invites the wrong conclusion and gives no next step.
    status: untested
    checked: null
    evidence: customer-contact

economics:
  currency: USD
  mrr: null
  monthly_cost: 0
  customers: null

budget:
  monthly_cap: 1
  protected: false

kill_criteria:
  - Fewer than three distinct GitHub users engage within 90 days of the page being reachable from the published site.
  - A report of script injection through a survey title, question or answer, a response stored from a closed survey, or an admin action accepted without the key.

links:
  production: https://duncan-haywood.github.io/monorepo-projects/survey-keeper/
  analytics: null

docker-compose.yml.text:
# Any box with Docker:
#   ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) docker compose up -d
# Put it behind HTTPS (Caddy, nginx, a tunnel) before real use.
services:
  survey-keeper:
    build: .
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports: ["8080:8080"]
    volumes: ["state:/data"]
    environment:
      ADMIN_KEY: ${ADMIN_KEY:?set ADMIN_KEY}
      STATE: /data/state.json
      TRUST_PROXY: ${TRUST_PROXY:-false}
      PUBLIC_URL: ${PUBLIC_URL:-}
      ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL: ${ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL:-}
      EMBED_ORIGINS: ${EMBED_ORIGINS:-}
volumes:
  state:

fly.toml.text:
# Fly.io self-deploy, in your own account (needs flyctl and a card on file with Fly):
#   fly launch --copy-config --no-deploy --dockerfile Dockerfile
#   fly volumes create state --size 1
#   fly secrets set ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16)
#   (optional settings from render.yaml, e.g. PUBLIC_URL, go in with `fly secrets set` too)
#   fly deploy
# One machine that never auto-stops: the state file lives on its volume.
app = "survey-keeper-CHANGE-ME"
primary_region = "iad"

[build]
  dockerfile = "Dockerfile"

[env]
  PORT = "8080"
  STATE = "/data/state.json"
  TRUST_PROXY = "true"

[mounts]
  source = "state"
  destination = "/data"

[http_service]
  internal_port = 8080
  force_https = true
  auto_stop_machines = "off"
  auto_start_machines = false
  min_machines_running = 1
  [[http_service.checks]]
    path = "/healthz"
    interval = "30s"
    timeout = "5s"

index.html.text:
An NPS survey that tells you why the score is what it is.

Survey Keeper is the open-source survey and Net Promoter Score server for a small product or shop. Define questions in plain text, share a link, and read results with a confidence range, the words detractors use more than promoters, and a score for each channel you sent it through. Below is the same calculation the server uses, running on sample answers you can replace. Everything on this page runs in your browser; nothing you type is uploaded.

Try it: paste scores and comments

—

What people mention

WordCommentsDetractors vs promoters

Word counting with common words removed, not a language model. A word detractors use at least 1.5 times as often as promoters is a place to look first.

Why someone would use this

TodayCatchSurvey Keeper
Typeform, SurveyMonkey, Delighted, SurvicateMonthly fees that rise with responses; answers live with them; the cheap tiers hide trend and exportYour server, unlimited surveys and responses, no per-response fee
LimeSurvey, FormbricksFull platforms: a database, a build, many settingsOne Node process and one JSON file
A Google Form and a spreadsheetNo NPS maths, no range, no per-channel score, no alert on an unhappy customerNPS, 95% range, results by ?ref= and a webhook on every detractor

Honest limits: no skip logic or page branching, no email sending (share the link or embed it), one admin key, no respondent panel, and the word table is counting, not sentiment analysis. For research-grade surveys, use a full platform.

Run it yourself

git clone https://github.com/Duncan-Haywood/oss-monorepo && cd oss-monorepo/ventures/survey-keeper
node --test
ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) node server.mjs

Open http://localhost:8080/admin (any user name, ADMIN_KEY as the password), edit the sample survey, and share /s/customer-pulse?ref=email. One-click Render deploy, Fly.io and Docker are in the README.

Questions

Why not just use Typeform, SurveyMonkey or Delighted?

Those are polished and the right call if you need logic branching, a design studio, panels of respondents or a vendor to call. They charge by the month, often cap responses on the cheaper plans, and your customers' answers live on their servers. Survey Keeper is one small Node server in your own account: NPS, rating, choice and free-text questions, results with a confidence range, CSV export and no per-response fee. It suits a product or shop that wants a pulse from a few hundred customers.

How is the NPS calculated, and what is the range?

Each answer counts as +1 for a 9 or 10, 0 for a 7 or 8 and -1 for 0 to 6. The score is the average times 100. The 95% range comes from the variance of that three-point score, so with 20 answers it is wide and with 400 it narrows. If a change moves the score by less than the range, you cannot tell it from noise.

What is the detractor-words table?

For every free-text question, Survey Keeper lists the words that come up in comments and shows whether detractors or promoters use each one more often. It is plain word counting with stop words removed, not a language model. A word like billing that detractors use several times as often as promoters points at what to fix first.

Can I paste scores I already have?

Yes. The demo on this page takes lines of a score and an optional comment, for example 9, fast and friendly, and shows the NPS, its range and the word table in your browser. Nothing you paste is uploaded.

How do I run a survey?

Define it in plain text, one question per line, such as nps*: How likely are you to recommend us? and text: What is the main reason for your score? Share the link, add ?ref=email or ?ref=app to see each channel's score, or embed it in an iframe from an origin you allow.

What does it store?

Your survey definitions and each response as the answers given, a timestamp and an optional short source tag, in one JSON file you control. It stores no name, email or IP address unless a respondent types one into a comment. IP addresses are held in memory only for rate limiting. You are the operator and responsible for your privacy notice and any consent your respondents' location requires.

Same builder, other jobs: Help Keeper runs a help center, Feedback Board collects feature requests, Form Inbox collects website forms and Support Desk answers customer email.

No warranty. This tool and the server are provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied, and with no uptime or delivery guarantee. You are the operator of any survey you run, responsible for its questions, a privacy notice and the data-protection and consent rules where you and your respondents live. The NPS, its range and the word table are heuristics, they depend on who answers, and they can be wrong. This is not legal, tax, or financial advice.

render.yaml.text:
# One-click self-deploy: https://render.com/deploy?repo=<your fork URL>
# Render builds the Dockerfile in YOUR account; nothing runs on the author's.
# No third-party key is required: the survey server has no outside dependencies.
services:
  - type: web
    name: survey-keeper
    runtime: docker
    dockerContext: ventures/survey-keeper
    dockerfilePath: ventures/survey-keeper/Dockerfile
    plan: starter
    healthCheckPath: /healthz
    disk:
      name: state
      mountPath: /data
      sizeGB: 1
    envVars:
      - key: STATE
        value: /data/state.json
      - key: TRUST_PROXY
        value: "true"
      - key: ADMIN_KEY
        generateValue: true
      - key: PUBLIC_URL
        sync: false
      - key: ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL
        sync: false
      - key: EMBED_ORIGINS
        sync: false
